record.original_question: If a meromorphic function with an omitted value has a quasi-nested wandering domain, must that function necessarily have no Herman rings?

evidence.quote: Chakraborty et al. [10] in 2022 proved that the existence of a quasi-nested wandering domain of a meromorphic function f with an omitted value ensures that there exists no unbounded Fatou component of f giving that an unbounded Herman ring does not exist for f. We make the following conjecture. Conjecture: Meromorphic functions with quasi-nested wandering domains have no Herman rings.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f: ℂ → ℂ ∪ {∞} be a transcendental meromorphic function, and let F(f) denote its Fatou set, i.e., the set of points z ∈ ℂ at which the family of iterates {f^n} is normal in some neighborhood. A connected component U of F(f) is called a wandering domain if the components U_n containing f^n(U) are pairwise disjoint for n = 0, 1, 2, …. Such a wandering domain U = U_0 is called quasi-nested if every U_n is bounded and there exists a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers {n_k} such that, for each k, the component U_{n_k} surrounds the origin (i.e., 0 lies in the bounded complementary component of U_{n_k}), and the spherical/Euclidean distance from U_{n_k} to ∞ tends to 0 as k → ∞ (equivalently, U_{n_k} → ∞).

A periodic Fatou component A of period p ≥ 1 is called a Herman ring if A is conformally a round annulus and f^p restricted to A is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of that annulus.

Prove or disprove: every transcendental meromorphic function f that possesses a quasi-nested wandering domain has no Herman ring (in any cycle of Fatou components).
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is posed as an open conjecture in recent surveys on Herman rings of meromorphic functions. A 2022 result establishes the implication only under the additional hypothesis that f has an omitted value (showing in fact the absence of unbounded Fatou components, hence no unbounded Herman ring). The general conjecture without the omitted-value hypothesis appears not to have been resolved.

status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture: Meromorphic functions with quasi-nested wandering domains have no Herman rings.

status_evidence.snippet: Existence of a quasi-nested wandering domain of a meromorphic function f with an omitted value ensures that there exists no unbounded Fatou component of f.
